emily: Hey runtime team — inbound from support: Customer 'AtlasCRM' reporting a sudden p99 latency spike on the /v1/generate endpoint starting ~2026-03-16T23:40Z. Baseline p99 ~220ms -> now ~950ms for sequences >1200 tokens. No increase in QPS. Error rate still low but tail latency kills SLA. Deploys around that time: attn-compileflag v2.3.9. tagging @sara @vikram

sara: thanks, emily. grabbing traces from their tenant. Do we have kernel selection logs for their requests?

vikram: I pulled trace ids 0x7f9a and 0x7f9b from their org. Looks like runtime selected flash-attn variant for many of the long-seq calls (unexpected). SDPA used to be preferred for >1024 but selection heuristics returned flash for these.

mike: interesting — there was a recent compileflag change that adjusted heuristics for small batch/longseq throughput. Maybe it inverted a sign in the threshold. I'll check commit 3f9c8 (attn heuristics).

sara: timeline: attn-compileflag v2.3.9 rolled at 2026-03-16T23:37:30. Telemetry ingestion shows a gap between 23:36 and 23:41 for kernel-selector metrics (we're missing recent per-kernel perf stats). If heuristic uses recent perf windows it might have defaulted to flash.

emily: customer says spike started exactly after our deploy, they sent sample request ids. Sharing below.

emily: sample log snippet from their request: ```
2026-03-16T23:40:12Z [req=0x7f9a] model=gpt-large seq_len=1342 batch=1 kernel=flash_attn time_ms=948
2026-03-16T23:40:12Z [req=0x7f9a] kv_cache_hits=0
2026-03-16T23:40:12Z [req=0x7f9b] model=gpt-large seq_len=1400 batch=1 kernel=flash_attn time_ms=1023
```

sara: those latencies line up with fallback path when flash handles longseq inefficiently. We need to confirm: did the kernel perf probe run during that deploy?

mike: the perf-prober runs every 10m; last successful probe before deploy was 23:31. The 23:36-23:41 ingestion gap prevented probes from updating the selection table. So heuristics had stale data and some new tie-break logic picks flash by default. Looks like a bug: newly-introduced tie-break favored flash when last_seen is older than 5m.

jin: mitigation options: 1) hotfix the tie-break to prefer SDPA for sequences >=1024 until fresh probes return; 2) roll back compileflag v2.3.9; 3) force per-tenant kernel override for AtlasCRM to SDPA; 4) temporary traffic split to older runtime pool. Thoughts?

sara: quick and low-risk: per-tenant override to SDPA for AtlasCRM while we push hotfix. We have admin API: `POST /admin/tenants/{id}/overrides` payload `{ "kernel_preference": "sdpa" }`

emily: go ahead and do override? customer asked for ETA ASAP.

vikram: I'm applying override now to tenant id `atlas-001` via admin console. Command: ```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/admin/tenants/atlas-001/overrides \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kernel_preference":"sdpa","reason":"emergency tail latency mitigation"}'
```

ci-bot: deploy job 5521 queued by vikram — applying tenant override (atlas-001).

ci-bot: deploy job 5521 succeeded — override applied on nodes: rtm-08, rtm-12, rtm-21.

emily: customer confirmed initial improvement: p99 dropped from ~950ms -> ~280ms within 2 minutes. They say errors still low.

mike: good signal. Next steps: revert tie-break bug in attn-compileflag, add unit test for tie-break logic, and make probe ingestion resilient to short gaps. Also add alert when kernel-selection telemetry gap > 30s.

jin: can we push a targeted hotfix to change default tie-break to prefer sdpa for seq>=1024 while we roll out tests? I'll file a small patch and cut a canary.

sara: repro steps for engineers to validate locally: 1) build runtime with `ATTN_HEURISTIC_DEBUG=1` 2) run `scripts/run_perf_probe.sh --model gpt-large --seq 1400 --batch 1` 3) run a short loadpipe: `ab -n 50 -c 1 https://rtm-canary.internal/v1/generate -H 'X-Tenant: atlas-001'` 4) inspect `/var/log/rtm/kernel_selector.log` for lines like `selected=flash_attn last_seen=2026-03-16T23:31`.

mike: I'm pushing a PR now: fix tie-break and add telemetry-gap alert (PR: github.com/redwood/rtm/pull/8214). Will request review from @sara and @vikram.

emily: support will message customer with summary and ETA. They asked for a postmortem once root cause and fix done.

vikram: monitoring plan: 1) rollback flag if p99 doesn't improve on canary, 2) monitor p95/p99, kernel selector success rate, perf-prober success ratio, and ingestion latency. I set an alert for 10% increase in p99 across tenants hitting seq>1024.

sara: adding to postmortem checklist: timeline, deploy id, affected tenants, mitigation steps, patch PR id, test added, and follow-up tasks (probe redundancy, tie-break unit tests).

emily: thumbs up — I'll kick off the incident doc and mark this as mitigated for AtlasCRM. Will keep thread open until PR merged and rollout completed. :thumbsup:
